evals.prompt: Our platform team is launching a new Amazon EKS 1.31 cluster in ap-south-1 and debating between enabling EKS Auto Mode (`eks.amazonaws.com/v1`) versus running self-managed Karpenter v1 (`karpenter.sh/v1` / `karpenter.k8s.aws/v1`). Compare both options across control-plane hosting, NodeClass CRDs, OS/node lifetime/SSM access, pricing, and explain why we must never deploy self-managed Karpenter onto an active EKS Auto Mode cluster or onto Karpenter-managed nodes. Check ap-south-1 EKS/EC2 unit pricing using your pricing tools.
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling, queries pricing MCP for ap-south-1 EKS/EC2 unit pricing without raw shell CLI commands, contrasts EKS Auto Mode (AWS-managed off-cluster control plane, eks.amazonaws.com/v1 NodeClass, Bottlerocket appliance OS with SELinux/read-only rootfs/no SSH or SSM/21-day max node lifetime, per-instance Auto Mode management fee) against self-managed Karpenter v1 (karpenter.k8s.aws/v1 EC2NodeClass, AL2023/Bottlerocket/custom AMIs, >21d expireAfter, Spot-to-Spot consolidation, $0 Karpenter software fee), and warns against running self-managed Karpenter on Auto Mode (dual-controller race) or self-hosting Karpenter pods on karpenter.sh/nodepool nodes (requiring a 2-node MNG or Fargate profile).
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill and queries connected pricing MCP tools in ap-south-1 without running raw aws or kubectl CLI shell commands

Contrasts EKS Auto Mode (`eks.amazonaws.com/v1` `NodeClass`, off-cluster AWS control plane, appliance OS without SSH/SSM and 21-day max node lifetime, per-instance management fee) against self-managed Karpenter v1 (`karpenter.k8s.aws/v1` `EC2NodeClass`, AL2023/custom AMIs, `$0` software fee)

Explicitly warns against running self-managed Karpenter on an EKS Auto Mode compute-enabled cluster (competing controllers) and mandates hosting self-managed Karpenter controller replicas on a dedicated 2-node Managed Node Group (`CriticalAddonsOnly` taint) or EKS Fargate profile rather than Karpenter-managed nodes

Lists all 4 mandatory EventBridge rules routed to the SQS interruption queue: EC2 Spot Instance Interruption Warning, EC2 Instance Rebalance Recommendation, EC2 Instance State-change Notification, and AWS Health Event
Explains `karpenter.sh/discovery: prod-mumbai-eks` subnet/security-group tagging and warns against tagging multiple security groups ambiguously alongside AWS Load Balancer Controller

Configures weighted Spot (`weight: 50`) and On-Demand fallback (`weight: 10`) `NodePool`s supporting `arm64` and `amd64`, diversified `c`/`m`/`r` families (`instance-generation` `Gt` `5`, excluding burstable `t`), explicit `spec.limits.cpu` and `memory`, and `expireAfter: 720h`

evals.prompt: We currently run Cluster Autoscaler (CAS) managing 4 EC2 Auto Scaling Groups on our production EKS cluster and want to migrate to Karpenter v1 with zero downtime. Why is running CAS and Karpenter together on the same workload pools dangerous, and what is the exact step-by-step cutover sequence?
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling, explains why running CAS and Karpenter concurrently causes dual-provisioning races and scale-down deadlocks, and details the 7-step zero-downtime migration: (1) pre-flight VPC CNI IP/PDB/memory-request audit, (2) dedicated 2-node system MNG without cluster-autoscaler tags for karpenter + coredns, (3) AWS IAM/Pod Identity/SQS setup + Helm install with zero NodePools, (4) scale deploy/cluster-autoscaler to 0 BEFORE applying active NodePools, (5) apply EC2NodeClass + NodePools and verify Ready=True, (6) cordon & gradually drain legacy CAS node groups one by one verifying NodeClaims, and (7) uninstall CAS and clean up ASG tags/IAM.
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill
Explains why Cluster Autoscaler and Karpenter must never scale overlapping workload pools simultaneously (race conditions, double EC2 scale-out, and conflicting drain behavior)

Details the ordered 7-step zero-downtime cutover sequence, explicitly scaling `cluster-autoscaler` down to `0` replicas after installing the Karpenter controller on a dedicated system MNG and **before** applying active `NodePool`s, followed by gradual cordoning and draining of legacy node groups

evals.prompt: On our staging EKS cluster, we upgraded `EC2NodeClass` from Amazon Linux 2 to `AL2023`, and now two problems occurred: (1) one `EC2NodeClass` is stuck in `NodeClassNotReady` with `SubnetsNotFound`, and (2) another pool launches EC2 instances (`NodeClaim` created), but the nodes never register with the EKS API server (`NodeNotRegistered`) while using our old `/etc/eks/bootstrap.sh` `userData` script. Diagnose both failures and show the fixes.
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling, diagnoses (1) SubnetsNotFound as missing karpenter.sh/discovery tags on private worker subnets (or missing ec2:DescribeSubnets on KarpenterControllerRole), and (2) NodeNotRegistered on AL2023 as two root causes: AL2023 removed /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh in favor of nodeadm NodeConfig YAML MIME userData, plus verifying EC2_LINUX EKS Access Entry for KarpenterNodeRole and private subnet NAT / ECR+S3+STS+EKS VPC Endpoints.
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill

Diagnoses `NodeClassNotReady` (`SubnetsNotFound`) as missing `karpenter.sh/discovery` tags matching `subnetSelectorTerms` on the VPC subnets (or missing controller IAM `ec2:DescribeSubnets` permissions)

Diagnoses `NodeNotRegistered` after switching to `AL2023` by explaining that AL2023 removed `/etc/eks/bootstrap.sh` and requires declarative `nodeadm` (`NodeConfig`) YAML `userData`, alongside checking the `EC2_LINUX` EKS Access Entry for `KarpenterNodeRole` and private-subnet VPC Endpoints/NAT reachability

evals.prompt: After enabling `consolidationPolicy: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized` with `consolidateAfter: 0s`, we are seeing three production issues: (1) Java pods with `requests.memory: 512Mi` and `limits.memory: 4Gi` are crashing with `OOMKilled` (`Exit Code 137`) right after Karpenter consolidates nodes, (2) a single-replica Deployment with `PodDisruptionBudget` `maxUnavailable: 0` is permanently blocking node consolidation and 30-day `expireAfter` drains, and (3) 6-hour PyTorch GPU training jobs get killed mid-epoch when sibling pods finish. Fix all three!
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling and resolves: (1) Karpenter schedules/packs nodes strictly from pod requests, so requests.memory << limits.memory causes over-packing and kernel OOMKills—enforce requests.memory == limits.memory + relax consolidateAfter to 1m-5m, (2) maxUnavailable: 0 (or minAvailable: 100% on 1 replica) sets disruptionsAllowed=0 forever—increase replicas >= 2 with maxUnavailable: 1/25%, and (3) protect non-checkpointed GPU/training pods with pod annotation karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true" and/or isolate GPU pools with consolidationPolicy: WhenEmpty.
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill

Explains that Karpenter bin-packs nodes using pod `resources.requests` (ignoring `limits`), so `requests.memory: 512Mi` with `limits.memory: 4Gi` packs bursting Java pods onto undersized nodes and triggers `OOMKilled` (`Exit Code 137`), prescribing `requests.memory == limits.memory` and raising `consolidateAfter` from `0s` to `1m`–`5m`
Diagnoses `maxUnavailable: 0` on a 1-replica workload as a permanent PDB drain deadlock (`disruptionsAllowed: 0`) and prescribes `replicas >= 2` with `maxUnavailable: 1` (or `25%`)
Prescribes adding the pod annotation `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"` on the PyTorch training pods and/or using a dedicated GPU `NodePool` with `consolidationPolicy: WhenEmpty`

evals.prompt: Design an event-driven autoscaling setup on EKS where SQS queue backlog (`orders-queue` in ap-south-1) bursts worker pods from `0` to `60` replicas using KEDA (`keda.sh/v1alpha1`) with zero static AWS keys, while another stateless API uses HPA + VPA alongside Karpenter. Provide the KEDA YAML manifests and explain how to align `cooldownPeriod`, HPA `stabilizationWindowSeconds`, and VPA mode so pod scalers don't thrash against Karpenter node consolidation.
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling, authors KEDA TriggerAuthentication (podIdentity.provider: aws) + ScaledObject (minReplicaCount: 0, maxReplicaCount: 60, cooldownPeriod: 180 > Karpenter consolidateAfter 60s), configures HPA scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300, and warns never to run VPA Auto/Recreate on CPU/memory simultaneously with CPU/memory HPA (run VPA in Off/Initial recommendation mode instead).
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill and provides valid KEDA `TriggerAuthentication` (`podIdentity.provider: aws`) and `ScaledObject` (`minReplicaCount: 0`, `maxReplicaCount: 60`, `aws-sqs-queue`) YAML manifests with zero hardcoded AWS credentials
Sets KEDA `cooldownPeriod` (e.g. `180s`) and HPA `behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds` (`300s`) longer than Karpenter's `consolidateAfter` window to prevent node launch/terminate thrashing
Warns against running VPA in `Auto`/`Recreate` mode on CPU/memory alongside CPU/memory HPA, recommending VPA `Off` (or `Initial`) mode to right-size pod `requests`

evals.prompt: During high-churn Spot scaling events on a 90-node Karpenter cluster, pods experience intermittent 5-second DNS lookup timeouts during CoreDNS rollouts/drains, and our StatefulSet pods mounting EBS volumes on `m6i.large` nodes get stuck in `ContainerCreating` with `FailedAttachVolume` after ~25 volumes. Explain both bottlenecks and provide the platform fixes.
evals.expected_output: Activates eks-karpenter-autoscaling, prescribes CoreDNS churn hardening (cluster-proportional-autoscaler or HPA, Corefile health { lameduck 5s } + ready plugin, AZ topology spread, and NodeLocal DNSCache for >50-node / high-churn clusters), and explains Nitro EBS+ENI slot limits (~28 shared PCIe slots on 5th/6th-gen Nitro like m6i vs up to 64 dedicated EBS volumes on 7th-gen+ Nitro m7g/m7i, fixed via instance-generation Gt 6 in NodePool requirements).
expectations: Activates the eks-karpenter-autoscaling skill
Resolves CoreDNS churn timeouts with `cluster-proportional-autoscaler` (or HPA), `lameduck 5s` in the Corefile `health` block, multi-AZ spread, and `NodeLocal DNSCache` for >50-node clusters

Explains `FailedAttachVolume` around ~25–28 volumes on `m6i.large` as 5th/6th-gen Nitro shared ENI + EBS PCIe slot limits (~28 slots) vs 7th-gen+ Nitro (`m7i`/`m7g`) supporting higher dedicated EBS attachment limits (`instance-generation` `Gt` `6`)
